mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 0.09% is at a historically low level, which has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. A low rate environment reduces the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to higher equity prices.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 235.0 (current value: 233.887) signals an inflationary shock that increases equity risk premiums and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 235.0), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.0% and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0, it signals a recessionary risk that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE>6.0 AND INDPRO<100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy rate increase leads to higher discount rates and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
